display.scope: Active pixel window (AA); separate from cover VA.

touchCover.scope: Native cover component bounding dimensions, including any attached flex; not a glass thickness claim.

screen.basis: Active dimensions from dimension-photo; located on the exposed native optical window. Internal simplified optical surfaces and AA/VA differences are separately documented.

inspectionGroups.notes: Debug separation of the native optical stack; not a manufacturer assembly/removal sequence.

dimensionTargets.scope: Native PCB dimensions after rigid transform.

materialBasis: Native sRGB colors where specified, optical surfaces darkened and PCB/brass categories photo-supported. Missing colors neutral or explicitly illustrative. No static UI used as framebuffer.
assemblyNotes: Native CAD millimetres; identity for native+Z fronts, proper Y180 and XY translation for C native-Z fronts. No omitted source components or inferred housing.
limitations: Each SKU uses its own explicitly named official STEP and mechanical drawing. All native solids, orphan shells and faces are retained; fine parts are grouped by material only. Shared part names or a shared schematic do not certify equivalent PCBs.

Runtime hardwareRevision is unspecified. STEP filename dates, optical-module part-name versions and photograph silkscreen are source evidence, not certification of the present electrical board revision or a product release date.
Native millimetres are preserved with a proper rigid transform only; no nonuniform scaling or inferred component relocation. Native source assembly overlaps are not Boolean-repaired.

BOOT alone is bound to the physically identified source key. RESET and the slide power switch remain visible source geometry; reset uses the platform action and no unverified GPIO power control is created.

The framebuffer is a separate live surface 0.008 mm in front of the native exposed optical window for rendering. This offset is not physical laminate thickness. AA dimensions and larger cover VA dimensions remain distinct.

Source photographs remain unchanged references. Approximate rear registration is a mechanical placement review, not calibration of factory text orientation relative to USB, hardware fit, or browser/WebGL acceptance.
External batteries, cables and other accessories are not included in the native assembly and have not been invented.

The C source front faces native -Z. A180-degree Y rotation plus XY translation presents the front at+Z with the connector/flex tail downward. This rigid mechanical presentation does not claim runtime text-to-USB calibration.
The native PCB is approximately66.002×65.372×1.6 mm. The73 mm circle is LCD glass, and the95.86 mm circle belongs only to the touch cover; neither is substituted for PCB width.
The non-touch resources page links a Touch-named schematic. This source naming conflict is recorded and is not treated as proof that touch and non-touch electrical material is identical.

The official touch-C front gallery image is byte-identical to the base2.1 front image (SHA256 b9e21f8c556ea15929e292b4d746702359089fd16444445b1a151db606b14260). It is retained as reused stock imagery, excluded from mechanical registration; the independent touch-C CAD, dimensions and rear photo define this model.

Exact touch dimension photograph gives AA70.13 mm; its independent mechanical PDF labels cover VA70.64 mm. Native cover VA face3 is used to locate the live window, with its own center. The internal LCD source lacks a separate AA face and is not transplanted from the non-touch assembly.

Native assembled depth is9.71048 mm versus the drawing reference9.7 mm. This source precision difference is retained. LCD/FPC component spans81.94490 mm; the77.59 mm separate non-touch main-body dimension is not imposed on it.

The primary square IC body visible on the upper rear in the exact official photograph is absent from this source assembly solid/shell/face topology. The native CAD is retained without inventing that package or its height; complete source-component coverage is not a claim of a complete physical BOM.
